item.title: Beyond the Screenshot: What Claims Professionals Should Expect From Digital Evidence Preservation
item.description: Federal Rule of Evidence 901 asks whether there is sufficient evidence to support a finding that an item is what its proponent claims it is. The more important question is what supporting information should be preserved so that the image can still be evaluated later. View Series Online evidence has a way of disappearing.

item.title: A Landmark Supreme Court Ruling Is Upending How America Moves Its Goods
item.description: A US Supreme Court decision in May changed the stakes for freight brokers like Ilg, opening them to lawsuits if a driver for a contracted carrier gets into a collision. Daniel Ilg started out in the freight brokerage industry at 14 years old, learning from his dad how to match trucking companies with loads of goods that needed to move around the country. The ruling leaves plenty of uncertainty about when a broker ultimately might be held responsible.

item.title: Blackstone multi-strat alternatives fund makes its second direct cat bond investment
item.description: Blackstone Alternative Asset Management, the hedge fund solutions unit of Blackstone, has now made a second direct investment into a catastrophe bond through one of its flagship muti-strat alternatives funds. Back in May 2025 we reported that the Blackstone Alternative Multi-Strategy Fund had made its first direct investment into a catastrophe bond , having previously only allocated to insurance-linked securities (ILS) via external ILS manager operated strategies. Which was why it was notable when the Blackstone Alternative Multi-Strategy Fund made its first direct cat bond investment in 2025.

item.title: UBS to marginally increase cat bond allocations, says remain attractive on relative basis
item.description: We continue to focus on trading-oriented managers who could benefit from higher market volatility and rising dispersion, particularly given record tight spreads.” Adding that, “For more neutral portfolios, we plan to marginally increase our allocations to catastrophe bonds within Reinsurance as they remain attractive relative to most carry strategies.” Which at this stage of the cycle when catastrophe bond pricing has normalised towards more average historical levels, is a real signal of the quality of the returns that are still possible from the asset class, particularly when considered on a relative basis to other comparable asset types. In a volatile market environment when some hedge fund and alternative strategies have suffered, UBS Asset Management’s team sees catastrophe bonds as one asset class worth increasing allocations to, given it the carry they can provide remains relatively attractive compared to other investments in credit and fixed income. The UBS Unifed Global Alternatives team explained, “In Credit / Income, we plan on marginally increasing allocations to corporate long / short.

item.title: BTG Pactual sets up SSPE (Brazil ILS structure) to issue Letras de Risco de Seguro (LRS)

item.title: AM Best revises AmericanAg’s rating outlook to positive
item.description: AM Best has moved the outlook on American Agricultural Insurance Company’s (AmericanAg) Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating (Long-Term ICR) to positive from stable, while maintaining the company’s Financial Strength Rating (FSR) at A (Excellent) and its Long-Term ICR at “a” (Excellent), with the outlook for the FSR remaining stable. The positive outlook for the Long-Term ICR reflects what AM Best described as continued progress in AmericanAg’s operating performance. AM Best said its ratings assessment reflects AmericanAg’s strongest balance sheet strength, adequate operating performance, neutral business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

item.title: P&C market softens further as premium decreases accelerate in Q2’26: The Council
item.description: A softening property and casualty market became clearer in the second half of 2026, as premium decreases across all account sizes accelerated to an average of 2.0% from 1.2% in the first quarter. The findings, according to The Council of Insurance Agents & Brokers’ Commercial Property/Casualty Market Report for Q2 2026, mark the second consecutive quarter of broad premium reductions across the industry. Rate relief was felt most significantly by large accounts, which experienced average premium decreases of 3.7% following a 2.7% decrease last quarter.

item.title: Clear Group acquires Lloyd’s wholesale broker NPP
item.description: Clear Group, the independent insurance intermediary, has acquired Newman Pearce & Partners LLP (NPP), a specialist Lloyd’s wholesale broker, further strengthening its presence in the London Market and accelerating its wholesale growth strategy. NPP is an independent Lloyd’s wholesale broker founded in 2019 by Gordon Newman, Neil Pearce and Colin Rogers. For Clear, this acquisition represents a significant milestone in its strategy to grow the company’s London wholesale operations.

item.title: Londoners Find ‘Horrendous’ Cracks in Their Homes After Successive Heat Waves
item.description: Londoners are facing historic levels of subsidence risk after five successive heat waves dried out the clay soil on which much of the city is built. On Reddit, people offered personal accounts telling of “ horrendous cracking ” in their homes, and “doors sticking” due to subsidence. Londoners have taken to social media to express their dismay.

item.title: KPMG Australia to Fire Hundreds of Workers as Crisis Deepens
item.description: Scandal-plagued KPMG Australia is cutting almost 400 jobs as it grapples with the fallout from allegations it misused confidential client information to win business and as demand for consulting services slows. Read more : KPMG Australia Scandal Widens After it Confirms Optus Data Was Misused “KPMG has reviewed its costs and future workforce needs in response to continued economic weakness, difficult market conditions and the impact of the firm’s conduct and whistleblower matters,” KPMG Australia said in the statement. Over the last few months, KPMG Australia has been battling the fallout from allegations it misused confidential information from companies including property developer Lendlease Group to win contracts with other corporate clients.

item.title: Former Virginia Insurance Agent Pleads Guilty to Fraud
item.description: A former Virginia insurance agent pled guilty last week to wire fraud related to a scheme to pocket the premiums he was paid for policies he sold. According to court documents, Thomas Robert Hoyt, of Melfa, told certain clients to pay premiums to him and that he would forward the payments to the insurance carriers for which he was an agent. In response to complaints, the Virginia Bureau of Insurance opened an investigation in June 2021.

item.title: Chief Specialty files trademark application
item.description: Chief Specialty Insurance Company has filed a trademark application for the name “Chief Specialty.” The August 13 filing covers insurance underwriting, including specialty insurance, as well as claims processing, claims administration, insurance administration, and the provision of specialty insurance information. The application is new and has not yet been assigned to an examiner. The applicant is based in Van Wert, Ohio.

item.title: Apollo Global Reveals Data Breach After Hackers Target Financial Firms
item.description: Asset manager Apollo Global Management suffered a data breach last month in which hackers stole some personal information, according to a letter on Friday. Internet intelligence data reviewed by Reuters had shown that hackers devised websites aimed at stealing passwords from employees of private equity firms and financial companies. financial institutions and other businesses that were recently targeted by ransom-seeking hackers who use phone calls to compromise their victims, Reuters reported earlier this month.

item.title: Tesla Recalls 3 Million EVs in China Over Door Handle Safety
item.description: and at least eight other automakers are recalling millions of cars in China over safety concerns with their door handles, a major step to address flaws that have led to vehicle entrapment and multiple fatalities. The total number of EVs being recalled for door handle-related safety risks from the nine carmakers reached about 4.27 million affected. The Tesla vehicles have electrically controlled handles that can stop working in some crashes, which “could hinder occupants from quickly opening the doors to escape and impede rescue efforts by those outside the vehicle, posing a safety hazard,” according to a statement from China’s State Administration for Market Regulation.

item.title: Judge Narrows Ben & Jerry’s Lawsuit Accusing Unilever of Silencing Social Activism
item.description: A federal judge on Friday dismissed major portions of a Ben & Jerry’s lawsuit accusing its former parent Unilever of trying to silence the ice cream maker’s social activism, dismantle its board and stop funding its namesake foundation. Ben & Jerry’s accused Unilever of violating the 2000 merger agreement by censoring its speech, which has included protests against the war in Gaza, and ousting a chief executive who supported the company’s social activism. District Judge Kevin Castel in Manhattan dismissed seven claims and part of an eighth in a 10-count complaint by Vermont-based Ben & Jerry’s, whose flavors include Cherry Garcia, Half Baked and Phish Food, and by various independent directors.

item.title: InEvo Re gets A- rating and stable outlook from AM Best
item.description: Credit ratings agency AM Best has assigned a Financial Strength Rating of A- (Excellent) and a Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating of “a-” (Excellent) to InEvo Re, a Bermuda-based specialist life reinsurer backed by Macquarie Asset Management, with a stable outlook. is a new entrant to the reinsurance market; it benefits from the operational support and investment expertise of Macquarie Group and Macquarie Asset Management, particularly in private credit and long-duration asset strategies aligned with its long-term liabilities.” According to Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), InEvo Re has the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalisation. Additionally, AM Best predicted that InEvo Re will achieve near-term profitability and maintain prudent expense management, creating a scalable operating platform to support future growth.

item.title: Broadstone hires Matthew Ford to lead its Insurance Advisory & Remediation division
item.description: Broadstone, an independent UK financial services consultancy, has announced the appointment of Matthew Ford as Head of its Insurance Advisory & Remediation division. I am delighted to be joining at this time and will use my experience working at both consultancies and insurance firms, to bring a strong market focus and deliver bespoke, client-relevant solutions as we expand our insurance sector business.” Tony Gusmao, CEO of Broadstone, added, “Matthew’s appointment to lead our growing Insurance Advisory & Remediation division reflects our continued investment in the strategically important insurance market. His appointment follows Lovell Minnick Partners’ strategic growth investment in Broadstone, announced in January 2025, to accelerate the expansion of its capabilities, particularly within its Insurance Advisory & Remediation division.

item.title: People Moves: Causey Names Myers New Deputy Chief at NCDOI
item.description: North Carolina’s insurance commissioner has named Chuck Myers to be chief deputy commissioner Oct. For the past three years, Myers has been deputy commissioner for the Louisiana Department of Insurance, over property and casualty insurance. Myers also helped restructure the Louisiana Fortified Homes Program and led the Title Insurance Working Group at the National Association of Insurance Commissioners, NC Commissioner Causey said in a bulletin.

item.title: TikTok Agrees to $400 Million Children’s Privacy Settlement
item.description: Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said the Justice Department’s priority “is ensuring that children are protected online and that companies entrusted with their personal information meet their legal obligations.” Under the settlement, TikTok will pay $300 million immediately and an additional $100 million upon entry of an order vacating a prior consent decree entered with the Federal Trade Commission in 2019 against TikTok’s predecessor, Musical.ly. TikTok and its Chinese parent company ByteDance on Friday agreed to a $400-million settlement to resolve the U.S. The Justice Department sued TikTok and ByteDance in 2024 for allegedly failing to protect children’s privacy, and illegally collecting their information.

item.title: Trump’s Environmental Rollbacks Are Being Struck Down by Courts
item.description: The Trump administration’s many steps to reshape and shrink the scope of federal environmental protection have been met with a flood of legal challenges from companies, environmental groups and state officials. Over the past three months, federal courts nationwide have delivered rulings in several cases centered on attempts by the Environmental Protection Agency to terminate billions of dollars in climate grants and roll back Biden-era air policies. “The Trump EPA is committed to following the law, and courts have affirmed our rules and actions in a variety of contexts,” said Hirsch.

item.title: Cleanup Underway After Tornadoes Touch Down in Delaware and New York’s Long Island
item.description: Cleanup efforts and damage assessment were underway Friday in Delaware’s capital and on Long Island, New York, after tornadoes touched down during storms that battered the Northeast with heavy rains and left dozens of people stranded in their cars during flash flooding. Weather service crews were going to view the Delaware and Long Island damage on Friday to determine the strengths and paths of the tornadoes. In other parts of New York, flooding caused part of the Long Island Expressway in Queens to close in both directions, according to New York City Emergency Management.

item.title: Manulife launches travel insurance app in ChatGPT
item.description: Manulife has launched a ChatGPT app that allows Canadian travelers to receive personalized CoverMe travel insurance quotes. Users answer questions about their age, province of residence, destination, travel dates and trip cost. Once a quote is generated, they can continue to CoverMe.com, where the information provided in ChatGPT carries over to the purchase process.

item.title: RiverStone takes on $1.6 billion of QBE reserves
item.description: RiverStone International has entered into loss portfolio transfer reinsurance agreements with QBE Insurance covering approximately $1.6 billion of reserves. The agreements expand the companies’ existing relationship and transfer responsibility for managing the legacy liabilities to RiverStone, providing QBE with greater certainty around the covered reserves. These transactions demonstrate the breadth of RiverStone International’s capabilities and the strength of our global platform in providing finality and certainty for complex long-tail liabilities.

item.title: Exzeo authorizes $25 million share buyback
item.description: Exzeo has authorized a program to repurchase up to $25 million of its common stock. The timing and size of any purchases will depend on factors including Exzeo’s share price, available liquidity, and market conditions. The authorization runs for one year and does not require Exzeo to repurchase any specific number of shares.

item.title: Sapiens files trademark for SapiensAI
item.description: Insurance software provider Sapiens has filed a US trademark application for “SapiensAI.” The August 13 application covers downloadable software, SaaS, and platform services using artificial intelligence across property and casualty, life and annuities, workers’ compensation, medical professional liability, and reinsurance. item.title: Piracy Observer Says Somali Incidents Rising as Navies Stretched
item.description: The world’s top maritime piracy observer said incidents off the coast of Somalia are on the rise again after a pair of fresh attacks this week — as two major regional conflicts stretch naval forces in the area thin. Naval authorities this week reported that a pair of ships were attacked by Somali pirates, adding to previous concerns about a rising number of incidents this year. Read more: Iran War Fuels Piracy Surge Off Somalia Coast, EU Agency Says Mody said the risk of attacks off the Somali coast remains much lower than in 2009 and 2010, when attacks frequently occurred far into the Indian Ocean and targeted much larger merchant vessels.

item.title: Teen Drops Lawsuit Against Meta, Google and Snap Ahead of Trial
item.description: A teen girl whose lawsuit was a test case in litigation accusing social media companies of deliberately addicting young people and fueling a mental health crisis dropped her claims against the owners of Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Snapchat on Thursday, according to a court filing. M-Y., had alleged the platforms’ owners — Meta Platforms, Google and Snap Inc.— contributed to her social media addiction, depression and self-harm. “This plaintiff had a significant mental health condition that pre-dated her use of social media, and it’s clear that many of these cases fit the same pattern,” Meta said in a statement, adding that it would vigorously defend against the remaining cases.

item.title: Georgia Man Charged in Burglary of NASCAR Driver Greg Biffle’s Home After Plane Crash
item.description: A Georgia man burglarized former NASCAR driver Greg Biffle’s home after learning Biffle and his family died in a plane crash, a North Carolina sheriff said Tuesday. Williams was being held without bond in Cobb County, Georgia, on suspicion of another home burglary. Terrell Williams, 44, has been charged with second-degree burglary, safe cracking, money laundering and other felonies, Iredell County Sheriff Darren Campbell announced at a news conference.

item.title: Abbott to Pay $670M to Settle Some Preterm Infant Formula Cases
item.description: Abbott did not admit liability in Thursday’s settlement, saying it remains confident in the safety of its infant formula products. Abbott said on Thursday it reached a $670 million settlement to partially resolve the ongoing litigation over alleged harms linked to its specialty formulas for preterm infants. The settlement was agreed to by three law firms representing about 2,000 people with claims against Abbott, including one Illinois mother who won a $495 million judgment in 2024 after a jury concluded that Abbott’s formula caused her daughter to develop necrotizing enterocolitis, a dangerous bowel disease.

item.title: Florida AG Charges 7 in $100M Workers’ Compensation Fraud Scheme
item.description: The defendants face charges that include Organized Scheme to Defraud, Operating as an Unlicensed Money Service Business, and Workman’s Compensation Fraud. Seven defendants were charged last week for their roles in a sophisticated, organized scam that used multiple shell construction corporations to defraud workers’ compensation insurers, operated an unlicensed money service business, and processed nearly $100 million in payroll, according to Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier. “This criminal enterprise systematically exploited Florida’s workers’ compensation system for personal gain,” said Attorney General James Uthmeier.

item.title: Returns drive investor appetite, third-party reinsurance capital increasingly important: AM Best
item.description: Solid returns generated by the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market in recent years have encouraged investors to maintain or increase their allocations, leading rating agency AM Best to highlight third-party reinsurance capital as an increasingly important part of global reinsurance capacity. “As a result, third-party capital continues to represent an increasingly important component of global reinsurance capacity,” the agency explained. As we highlighted in a previous article, AM Best and reinsurance broker Guy Carpenter have raised their end of 2025 figure for third-party reinsurance capital, from the previous estimate of $120 billion to now $123 billion, while forecasting continued growth to $130 billion by the end of 2026.

item.title: Allianz Commercial hires Emma Woolley as President of Global Specialty & UK Region
item.description: Emma Woolley is set to join Allianz Commercial as President Global Specialty and UK Region, and will also join the Allianz Global Corporate & Specialty SE Board of Management, reporting to Thomas Lillelund, Chief Executive Officer (CEO), Allianz Commercial. Subject to regulatory approval, Woolley will join Allianz once her current professional commitments have ceased, no later than February 2027, and will take charge of Allianz Commercial’s Global Specialty lines of business and the UK markets. Woolley is expected to work closely with the insurer’s regional Presidents to expand Allianz’s Specialty portfolio globally, as well as with its Chief Underwriting Officer, Vanessa Maxwell Neverton, and Chief Distribution Officer, Jeremy Sharpe.
